title: Pass by const lvalue reference
recap: Pass by const reference avoids copying a potentially expensive object while preventing mutation through that parameter. The caller still owns the object and must keep it alive during the call.
Choose a value for cheap scalar inputs and a const reference when borrowing larger owned objects. The interface should express whether the function borrows, copies, or mutates.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Practice pass by const lvalue reference.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Implement longerThan(text,limit), true only when the string length is strictly greater than limit. The string is passed by const reference; do not copy or mutate it. Empty strings and limit zero are valid.
hints: Return a boolean without constructing another string.
